sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Shared logger setup
sections.what: Creates the single logger object the server writes through. Outside production it prints coloured, readable lines. In production it prints plain structured lines. It also removes authorization and cookie headers from anything it logs.
sections.why: Likely reason: one shared logger keeps output consistent, and hiding credentials keeps secrets out of log files.
sections.watch_out: A new header or field that carries a secret must be added to the redact list, or it will be logged.

summary: Creates the one shared logger the API server uses to write messages, and hides credential headers from those messages.
purpose: Give every part of the server one consistent way to write log lines.
why: Likely reason: readable coloured output while developing, and plain structured output in production. The redaction list is there so credentials do not land in logs.
how: Reads the log level from the LOG_LEVEL setting, defaults to info, hides authorization and cookie headers, and pretty-prints only when NODE_ENV is not production.
inputs: The LOG_LEVEL and NODE_ENV environment settings.
outputs: Log lines written to the console through the exported logger object.
risks: The redaction list covers only three header paths. Other secrets in logged objects are not hidden. Pretty printing depends on the pino-pretty package being installed outside production.
debug: If logs are too quiet or too noisy, check LOG_LEVEL. If coloured output appears in production, check NODE_ENV. If startup fails with a transport error, check that pino-pretty is installed.
